newsitem.title: UK: Battle for European Privatisation fund intensifies.
newsitem.headline: Battle for European Privatisation fund intensifies.

text.p: The battle over the corpse of the 500 million pound ($777.6 million) Kleinwort European Privatisation Investment Trust intensified on Friday as bidder TR European challenged the board to come clean on how much its deal is really worth.
"Let KEPIT's board give an illustration what they are really offering shareholders in pounds and pence," said Bob Cowdell of Hoare Govett, advisor to the TR European Growth Fund.
TR European is offering 103.1 pence for shares and warrants if holders opt for cash, or the equivalent of 107.6 pence if they choose to take TR European shares.
However, KEPIT which is also offering a cash exit via a money market unit trust, questions the terms TR would achieve from what could be the largest ever single sale of European equities.

KEPIT also says that it is impossible to put a price on the disposal of a portfolio which would be sold two months from now, but argues that it can get terms which are just as good and is offering 10 million pounds less in costs than TR European.

"TR European knows that it is unlikely ever to have to prove what it could get for the sale, but whatever they can get, so can we and our costs are going to be less, which means more money for shareholders," said Simon White a KEPIT director.

The 77,000 people who in 1994 subscribed to the dream of a European encore to Britain's give-away privatisation programme are also being offered a choice between the TR fund or a general European equity fund from M&G and a new Kleinwort privatisation trust with KEPIT's board recommending the latter two options.

"TR European is an aggressively managed fund and may be too risky for most small investors. Its portfolio is heavily concentrated and to compare that fund with a general Europe fund managed by M&G is not apples and pears," said KEPIT's White.

The pressure on fund managers to generate performance was thrown in to the limelight last week when Morgan Grenfell Asset Management suspended trading in three unit trusts over alleged irregularities involving investments in unquoted companies.
However, Bob Cowdell rejects the comparison between TR European, which is managed by Stephen Peak, and Morgan Grenfell.

"To impose this slur on Stephen is outrageous. TR European has less than one percent in unquoted stocks and it is not just the best performing European investment trust over the past year, but every year for the past five years," he said.
He also notes that after the poor performance of KEPIT, shareholders are unlikely to choose to invest in a new European privatisation investment vehicle managed by Kleinwort Benson.
"Look at the figures, TR European's net asset value is up 28.4 percent in the past year, 43.2 percent over two years and 148 percent over five," Cowdell said.

KEPIT is up 1.5 percent in one year and 11.3 percent in the two years since its formation, while M&G Europe & General is up 7.3 percent over one year, 16.6 percent over two and 89.7 percent over five.
Despite this, KEPIT believes that most shareholders will not accept the TR European offer.

"When they announce their first acceptances on Monday, it will be an embarassingly small percentage of shareholders. What the board has done is consider carefully all the options and we refuse to be pushed into making quite unrealistic estimates," said White.
